# Hosea Chapter 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 330v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/HOS_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1** The LORD gave this message to Hosea son of Beeri during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and during the reign of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.

**2** When the LORD first began speaking to Israel through Hosea, he said, "Go and marry a promiscuous woman and have children with her. For this land has been unfaithful to the LORD, chasing after other gods." **3** So Hosea married Gomer, daughter of Diblaim, and she became pregnant and gave him a son.

**4** The LORD said, "Name the boy Jezreel, for I am about to punish King Jehu's dynasty for the massacre at Jezreel. In fact, I will bring an end to the kingdom of Israel."

**6** She became pregnant again and gave birth to a daughter. The LORD said, "Name her No-Mercy. For I will show no more mercy to the people of Israel or forgive them."

**8** After Gomer had weaned No-Mercy, she again became pregnant and gave birth to a son. **9** The LORD said, "Name him Not-My-People. For Israel is not my people, and I am not their God."

**10** "Yet the time will come when Israel's people will be like the sands of the seashore — too many to count! Then, in the very place where they were told, 'You are not my people,' they will be called 'children of the living God.' **11** The people of Judah and Israel will be reunited, and they will choose one leader for themselves. What a day that will be — the day of Jezreel — when God will plant his people in his own land!"

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

Hosea 1 continues the prophet's exploration of the marriage metaphor — YHWH as the faithful husband, Israel as the unfaithful wife. The chapter's power lies in the intersection of personal pain and national theology.

*— PNEUMA*
